_: Kill-check for `asc standing-costs` (asc-09wx.11). Every mutant here is an attribution rule that a plausible implementation would get wrong: a character count where EV-54 measured bytes, `content` where it measured `stdout`, a record counted once instead of once per file, a first command taken from a segment that did not run, a hook wrapper matched anywhere in the text, and a set difference replaced by a subtraction. Each killer was found by planting the mutant and reading the failing names off assertionResults, not guessed. The invariants in the test file are the second line of defence: they compare the per-report totals against the report they must reconcile with, so an attribution that merely shifts bytes between two correct rows still fails.

killers.test: measures UTF-8 bytes across every file of one instructions record, and loads per file

mutants.find: const source = typeof stdout === 'string' ? stdout : attachment['content'];

killers.test: sizes hook_success by stdout, names the channel, and says so when it had to use content
measures UTF-8 bytes across every file of one instructions record, and loads per file

mutants.find: if (Array.isArray(blocks)) for (const block of blocks) total += byteLength(block);
